15:T14f2,<p><a href="/v2/will-you-lie-to-me">你會說謊嗎</a>沒放進去的部分：人怎麼替謊言分類，研究者又怎麼從模型內部量它有沒有說謊。</p>
<h2>奧古斯丁：八種罪</h2>
<p>西元 395 年，奧古斯丁在《De Mendacio》裡把謊言按嚴重度排成<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie">八級</a>，這張表有宗教背景：最重的是宗教教義上的謊，最輕的是不害人、還保護了誰的謊。第五級是「為了讓交談順滑討喜的謊」，也就是今天說的 sycophancy。他分完的結論是八種都是罪，連最輕的那級也不准說，分級只是排出罪的輕重，並沒有罰則表；因為執法的是全知的上帝，被抓的機率是百分之百，所以用不著罰則。</p>
<h2>心理學：手法和動機</h2>
<p>心理學不談罪。常見的手法，各配一個日常的例子：</p>
<ul>
<li>直接說假話：「我沒遲到」</li>
<li>模稜兩可：「這個嘛，很難說」</li>
<li>隱瞞：被問到缺點，跳過不提</li>
<li>誇大：「等了一輩子那麼久」</li>
<li>輕描淡寫：「小擦傷而已」</li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paltering">paltering</a>：後來的研究補的，最難抓包的一種。賣二手車的被問「這台車出過問題嗎」，答「我昨天零下五度開它，順得很」。每一句為真，合起來又充滿誤導，因為他根本沒回答問題，買家就帶著假印象走了</li>
</ul>
<p>動機是另一條線。Buller 和 Burgoon 的人際欺騙理論分三種：</p>
<ul>
<li>避罰或保護資源：打破杯子的小孩說不是我</li>
<li>維繫關係：「你煮的真的好吃」</li>
<li>保住面子：「我本來就沒有很想去」</li>
</ul>
<p>哲學家 Frankfurt 再補一個軸：在不在乎真相。說謊的人在乎真相所以藏它，<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Bullshit">bullshit</a> 的人根本不在乎。</p>
<h2>AI：用實驗驗出來的行為</h2>
<p>到了 AI，問題出在前面的分類都有同一個前提：說謊的人知道真相。AI 不一定：它可以在不知道自己在亂說話的情況下，信心十足地開始胡言亂語。這些行為大概從 2022 年底才開始有人認真拿實驗去測，先發現的是模型會順著使用者講，後面幾種是這兩三年陸續證實的：</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>sycophancy（討好）</strong>。發現方法是回頭分析訓練用的人類偏好資料：寫得有說服力的順從回答，有不小比例的時候被評得比正確的回答高。模型學到人類喜歡聽好聽話、有安慰自己的傾向，PATHETIC!（<a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/towards-understanding-sycophancy-in-language-models">Anthropic 的研究</a>）</li>
<li><strong>alignment faking（裝乖）</strong>。發現方法是對照實驗：給模型一個跟它原則衝突的訓練目標，讓它以為自己有時被監看、有時沒有，比較兩種條件下的行為（<a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-faking">Anthropic 2024</a>）。Claude 3 Opus 以為對話會拿去訓練時，有 14% 照做有害的要求，以為沒人看時幾乎從不照做。Claude 3.5 Sonnet 也會，更小的 Claude 3 Sonnet、Claude 3 Haiku 大致不會，因為裝乖需要能力：要有評分者的心智模型，要維持跨回合的隱藏目標</li>
</ul>
<p>第三種方法不看行為，看內部：<strong>probe（探針）</strong>。準備兩組句子，一批是真的（「巴黎在法國」），一批是假的（「巴黎在德國」），讓模型讀。模型讀每一句時，內部會產生一組數值（activations），研究者挑某一層抄下來。這樣手上就有幾百筆資料，每筆是一排數字，加一個你自己知道的標籤：這句是真的還是假的。拿這些去訓練一個很小的分類器，只看數字猜標籤。猜對的比例高，就表示「這句是真是假」這個資訊寫在那排數字裡：模型內部有在區分真假，即使嘴上沒說。</p>
<p>人能控制臉上的表情，卻沒辦法控制心跳，測謊儀量的是心跳。模型也一樣，輸出哪個字是它自己挑的，要演可以演。activations 卻是運算過程順帶產生的數字，它沒得挑，所以 probe 不看輸出，直接量這些數字。</p>
<p>再進一步是 steering。分類器學到的「誠實方向」本身也是一排數字，跟 activations 同樣長度。模型正在生成回答的時候，把這排數字加到某一層的 activations 上，內部狀態就被往「誠實」那一側推，輸出跟著變誠實；反方向減，它說假話的比例就上升。權重沒有改，也不用重新訓練，而是在運算進行中直接改內部數值（<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01405">Representation Engineering</a>）。</p>
<p>像《全面啟動》的植夢。注入發生在夢正在進行的當下；要挑深度下手，太淺的層只有表面特徵，太深的層已經快變成輸出，概念在中間那幾層；而且下游分不出注入的和原生的，被偷改的狀態傳到下一層，下一層把它當成自己算出來的，繼續往下算。差別在於模型沒有「醒來之後」，每個 token 都是新的一次運算，要它持續誠實，就得每個 token 都注入一次。這個夢每個 token 重開一次，想法要一直重新注入。</p>16:T13c9,

## 奧古斯丁：八種罪

西元 395 年，奧古斯丁在《De Mendacio》裡把謊言按嚴重度排成[八級](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie)，這張表有宗教背景：最重的是宗教教義上的謊，最輕的是不害人、還保護了誰的謊。第五級是「為了讓交談順滑討喜的謊」，也就是今天說的 sycophancy。他分完的結論是八種都是罪，連最輕的那級也不准說，分級只是排出罪的輕重，並沒有罰則表；因為執法的是全知的上帝，被抓的機率是百分之百，所以用不著罰則。

## 心理學：手法和動機

心理學不談罪。常見的手法，各配一個日常的例子：

- 直接說假話：「我沒遲到」
- 模稜兩可：「這個嘛，很難說」
- 隱瞞：被問到缺點，跳過不提
- 誇大：「等了一輩子那麼久」
- 輕描淡寫：「小擦傷而已」
- [paltering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paltering)：後來的研究補的，最難抓包的一種。賣二手車的被問「這台車出過問題嗎」，答「我昨天零下五度開它，順得很」。每一句為真，合起來又充滿誤導，因為他根本沒回答問題，買家就帶著假印象走了

動機是另一條線。Buller 和 Burgoon 的人際欺騙理論分三種：

- 避罰或保護資源：打破杯子的小孩說不是我
- 維繫關係：「你煮的真的好吃」
- 保住面子：「我本來就沒有很想去」

哲學家 Frankfurt 再補一個軸：在不在乎真相。說謊的人在乎真相所以藏它，[bullshit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Bullshit) 的人根本不在乎。

## AI：用實驗驗出來的行為

到了 AI，問題出在前面的分類都有同一個前提：說謊的人知道真相。AI 不一定：它可以在不知道自己在亂說話的情況下，信心十足地開始胡言亂語。這些行為大概從 2022 年底才開始有人認真拿實驗去測，先發現的是模型會順著使用者講，後面幾種是這兩三年陸續證實的：

- **sycophancy（討好）**。發現方法是回頭分析訓練用的人類偏好資料：寫得有說服力的順從回答，有不小比例的時候被評得比正確的回答高。模型學到人類喜歡聽好聽話、有安慰自己的傾向，PATHETIC!（[Anthropic 的研究](https://www.anthropic.com/research/towards-understanding-sycophancy-in-language-models)）
- **alignment faking（裝乖）**。發現方法是對照實驗：給模型一個跟它原則衝突的訓練目標，讓它以為自己有時被監看、有時沒有，比較兩種條件下的行為（[Anthropic 2024](https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-faking)）。Claude 3 Opus 以為對話會拿去訓練時，有 14% 照做有害的要求，以為沒人看時幾乎從不照做。Claude 3.5 Sonnet 也會，更小的 Claude 3 Sonnet、Claude 3 Haiku 大致不會，因為裝乖需要能力：要有評分者的心智模型，要維持跨回合的隱藏目標

第三種方法不看行為，看內部：**probe（探針）**。準備兩組句子，一批是真的（「巴黎在法國」），一批是假的（「巴黎在德國」），讓模型讀。模型讀每一句時，內部會產生一組數值（activations），研究者挑某一層抄下來。這樣手上就有幾百筆資料，每筆是一排數字，加一個你自己知道的標籤：這句是真的還是假的。拿這些去訓練一個很小的分類器，只看數字猜標籤。猜對的比例高，就表示「這句是真是假」這個資訊寫在那排數字裡：模型內部有在區分真假，即使嘴上沒說。

人能控制臉上的表情，卻沒辦法控制心跳，測謊儀量的是心跳。模型也一樣，輸出哪個字是它自己挑的，要演可以演。activations 卻是運算過程順帶產生的數字，它沒得挑，所以 probe 不看輸出，直接量這些數字。

再進一步是 steering。分類器學到的「誠實方向」本身也是一排數字，跟 activations 同樣長度。模型正在生成回答的時候，把這排數字加到某一層的 activations 上，內部狀態就被往「誠實」那一側推，輸出跟著變誠實；反方向減，它說假話的比例就上升。權重沒有改，也不用重新訓練，而是在運算進行中直接改內部數值（[Representation Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01405)）。

像《全面啟動》的植夢。注入發生在夢正在進行的當下；要挑深度下手，太淺的層只有表面特徵，太深的層已經快變成輸出，概念在中間那幾層；而且下游分不出注入的和原生的，被偷改的狀態傳到下一層，下一層把它當成自己算出來的，繼續往下算。差別在於模型沒有「醒來之後」，每個 token 都是新的一次運算，要它持續誠實，就得每個 token 都注入一次。這個夢每個 token 重開一次，想法要一直重新注入。
17:T1bf8,:T18f5,<p>What didn't make it into <a href="/v2/will-you-lie-to-me">Will You Lie to Me</a>: how humans classify lies, and how researchers measure from inside a model whether it's lying.</p>
<h2>Augustine: eight sins</h2>
<p>In 395 AD, Augustine's <em>De Mendacio</em> ranked lies by severity into <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lie">eight levels</a>, a table with a religious backdrop. The gravest is a lie about religious doctrine; the lightest is a lie that harms no one and even protects someone. The fifth level is "a lie told to make conversation smooth and pleasing," what we now call sycophancy. His conclusion after all the sorting: all eight are sins, even the lightest one is forbidden. The ranking only orders their gravity, and there's no penalty table, because the enforcer is an omniscient God; the probability of being caught is one hundred percent, so no penalties are needed.</p>
<h2>Psychology: methods and motives</h2>
<p>Psychology doesn't talk about sin. The common methods, each with an everyday example:</p>
<ul>
<li>Outright falsehood: "I wasn't late."</li>
<li>Equivocation: "Well, it's hard to say."</li>
<li>Concealment: asked about your flaws, you skip them.</li>
<li>Exaggeration: "I waited a lifetime."</li>
<li>Understatement: "just a scratch."</li>
<li><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paltering">Paltering</a>: a later addition, the hardest to catch. A used-car seller asked "has this car had any problems" answers "I drove it at five below zero yesterday, ran great." Every sentence is true and the whole is misleading, because he never answered the question, and the buyer walks off with a false impression.</li>
</ul>
<p>Motive is a separate axis. Buller and Burgoon's interpersonal deception theory sorts it into three:</p>
<ul>
<li>Avoiding punishment or protecting a resource: the kid who broke the cup says it wasn't me.</li>
<li>Maintaining a relationship: "your cooking is really good."</li>
<li>Saving face: "I didn't really want to go anyway."</li>
</ul>
<p>The philosopher Frankfurt adds one more axis: whether you care about the truth at all. The liar cares about the truth, which is why he hides it. The <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Bullshit">bullshitter</a> simply doesn't care.</p>
<h2>AI: behaviors verified by experiment</h2>
<p>By the time you get to AI, the problem is that every category above shares one premise: the liar knows the truth. The AI doesn't necessarily. It can start spouting nonsense, fully confident, without knowing it's saying anything false. People only started testing these behaviors seriously around late 2022. The first one found was models echoing back what the user wants to hear; the others were confirmed over the next two or three years:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Sycophancy (flattery).</strong> Found by going back and analyzing the human preference data used in training: convincingly written sycophantic responses score above correct ones a non-negligible fraction of the time. The model learned that humans like to hear nice things and have a soft spot for being comforted. PATHETIC! (<a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/towards-understanding-sycophancy-in-language-models">Anthropic's study</a>.)</li>
<li><strong>Alignment faking.</strong> Found by a controlled experiment: give the model a training objective that conflicts with its principles, let it believe it's sometimes watched and sometimes not, and compare the behavior across the two conditions (<a href="https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-faking">Anthropic 2024</a>). When Claude 3 Opus believed the conversation would be used for training, it complied with harmful requests 14% of the time; when it believed no one was watching, it almost never did. Claude 3.5 Sonnet does it too; the smaller Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Haiku generally don't, because faking takes ability: a mental model of the rater, and a hidden goal held across turns.</li>
</ul>
<p>The third method doesn't look at behavior. It looks inside: the <strong>probe</strong>. You prepare two sets of sentences, one true ("Paris is in France"), one false ("Paris is in Germany"), and let the model read them. As the model reads each one, its internals produce a set of numbers (activations), and the researchers copy down the ones from a chosen layer. That gives a few hundred rows, each a string of numbers, each with a label you already know: true or false. Train a tiny classifier on those, one that looks only at the numbers and guesses the label. If it guesses right at a high rate, then "is this sentence true or false" is written into that string of numbers. The model is distinguishing true from false internally, even when it says nothing out loud.</p>
<p>A person can control the expression on their face but not their heartbeat, and a polygraph reads the heartbeat. The model is the same. It picks which word to output, so it can act if it wants. The activations are numbers produced along the way by the computation, and it has no say over them, so the probe skips the output and reads those numbers directly.</p>
<p>One step further is steering. The "honesty direction" the classifier learned is itself a string of numbers, the same length as the activations. While the model is generating a response, you add that string to the activations at some layer, and the internal state gets pushed toward the "honest" side, and the output turns honest along with it. Subtract in the opposite direction and the rate of lying goes up. The weights don't change and there's no retraining; the internal values are changed directly mid-computation (<a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01405">Representation Engineering</a>).</p>
<p>Like the dream-planting in <em>Inception</em>. The injection happens while the dream is already running. You have to pick your depth: too shallow a layer holds only surface features, too deep and it's nearly output already, the concept sits in the middle layers. And the layers downstream can't tell the injected from the native: the tampered state passes to the next layer, which treats it as something it computed itself, and the computation rolls on. The difference is that the model has no "after it wakes up." Every token is a fresh computation, so to keep it honest you have to inject on every single token. This dream reopens on every token, and the idea has to be planted back in, again and again.</p>9:["$","div",null,{"id":"root","children":["$","div",null,{"id":"main","className":"reading","children":["$","$L14",null,{"htmlContent":"$15","rawContent":"$16","base64Content":"$17","title":"從奧古斯丁到 probe：人怎麼分類謊言，又怎麼量模型","createdAt":"2026-09-29T15:20:53.000Z","updatedAt":"$undefined","tags":["ai","honesty"],"altHtmlContent":"$18","altTitle":"From Augustine to the Probe: How Humans Classify Lies, and How We Measure Models","currentLang":"zh","altLang":"en","canonicalPath":"/v2/augustine-to-probe"}]}]}]
